Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Transient stimulus with long-term chromatin accessibility tracking
ideas.description: Expose cells to a brief AP-1-activating stimulus (e.g., TPA, injury, or cytokine), then run longitudinal ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN for AP-1 factors (FOS, JUN) and H3K27ac at days to weeks after withdrawal. Persistent AP-1 motif-enriched accessible regions after the stimulus has cleared, and not in naive cells, would indicate AP-1-dependent epigenetic memory.

ideas.title: Acute degron-based depletion at distinct time windows
ideas.description: Use auxin- or dTAG-inducible degradation of AP-1 components (e.g., FOS, JUNB, or dominant-negative A-FOS) during the priming phase versus the maintenance phase, then challenge cells with a second stimulus. If depletion during priming abolishes the enhanced secondary response but depletion during maintenance does not, AP-1 is needed to establish but not maintain memory, and the reverse pattern would show it is needed for maintenance.

ideas.title: Primed vs. naive re-stimulation transcriptional response
ideas.description: Compare RNA-seq and nascent transcription (PRO-seq/TT-seq) after a first versus second stimulus, with varying rest intervals between them, in wild-type and AP-1-perturbed cells. Faster or stronger induction of the same genes on re-challenge, with a decay constant that depends on AP-1 dosage, would quantify memory strength and duration.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome and live-cell reporter of AP-1 dynamics and heritability
ideas.description: Combine single-cell RNA+ATAC with live imaging of fluorescent AP-1 activity reporters (or endogenously tagged FOS/JUN) and lineage tracing, to follow primed cells through divisions. Heritable inheritance of AP-1 state and accessibility in daughter cells, and correlation between a cell's past AP-1 activity and its later response, would show whether memory is cell-autonomous and mitotically stable.

ideas.title: Site-specific causal perturbation of AP-1 motifs at memory loci
ideas.description: Use CRISPR base editing or deletion of AP-1 motifs at candidate memory enhancers, along with dCas9-based recruitment or blockade of AP-1 or chromatin remodelers like BAF, then test whether accessibility persistence and enhanced re-induction are lost. Also test sufficiency by inserting AP-1 sites into a naive locus and examining whether it retains accessibility after transient AP-1 activation, to separate AP-1 as a driver from AP-1 as a passive marker.
